title: From subvarieties to classes
mathematical_role: Explain the cycle-class map from codimension-p algebraic cycles to Hodge classes and isolate the conjectural surjectivity direction.
learning_objective: See the difference between algebraic cycles producing (p,p) cohomology classes, the many-to-one nature of the map, rational coefficients, and the open converse.
literal_semantics: The predecessor intends an arrow from geometric/algebraic input to an H^(p,p) target.
nonliteral_semantics: The source circle is not a specific variety or codimension-p subvariety.
The target rectangle is not the full cohomology group or its rational intersection.
The arrow does not encode injectivity or surjectivity.
No visible multiplicity or dimension is literal.

notes: Successor should distinguish Z^p(X), cl^p, H^{2p}(X,Q) intersect H^{p,p}(X), necessary algebraicity direction, and conjectural rational surjectivity.

reproducibility_notes: The predecessor is a conceptual icon rather than an explicit cycle-class diagram tied to a worked variety.

accessibility.alt_text: Algebraic subvarieties map through the cycle-class map into rational Hodge classes.
accessibility.long_description: The predecessor contains a generic source shape, an arrow, and an H^(p,p) target. The successor should show the domain of algebraic cycles, codimension p, the cycle-class map, the rational Hodge-class target, information lost by the map, and the open surjectivity boundary.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: Pedagogical exposition of the established direction from algebraic cycles to (p,p) classes and the location of the open rational converse.
not_claimed: A proof of the Hodge conjecture

supersession_reason: The conceptual arrow is valid but too impoverished to carry the theorem-critical coefficient, codimension, and surjectivity distinctions.
